description: Dino Runner online free: sprint across the desert, jump the cacti and duck under the pterodactyls. It starts slow and gets faster — how far can your dino go?
lede: The endless runner classic, in your browser. A little green dino sprints across a sunny desert that never ends, and the only controls are jump and duck. Cacti block the ground — leap over them. Pterodactyls swoop at head height — duck under the low ones and run under the high ones. It starts at a gentle jog and gets faster with every 100 points, so the run always ends in a trip. The question is only how far you get first.

p: Press Start running and the dino takes off on its own — you never steer it, you only jump and duck. Tap the game, press Space, or hit the big JUMP button to leap. A jump clears a cactus or a cluster of cacti, but the higher the jump, the longer you are in the air, so tap late and low for a single cactus and early for a wide cluster.

Pterodactyls fly at two heights. A low one swoops at head height: hold Arrow Down or the DUCK button and the dino flattens itself until the bird passes. A high one flies above the dino's head, so just keep running underneath it. Your score is the distance you ran, one point per metre, with a fanfare every 100 points.

Every metre you run is one point, so a score of 250 means 250 metres. There are no coins or power-ups — the only reward is distance, and the only enemy is speed. The dino starts at a gentle jog and speeds up with your score: at 100 points it runs about 20% faster than at the start, and by 700 points it is at full sprint, nearly two and a half times the starting speed.
The game ends the moment you touch a cactus or a bird. There is no second chance and no shield — but your best distance is saved in this browser, so every run is a chance to beat it.

sections.h: From the browser to the desert
p: The running dinosaur began as the Chrome offline game: when Google's browser lost its connection, a little pixel T-Rex appeared on the error page, and pressing Space started it running across a black-and-white desert. It was added in 2014, and by 2018 Google said it was played 270 million times a month — mostly by people whose internet had just dropped.

The idea stuck because the rule fits in one sentence: jump the cacti, duck the birds. No tutorial, no buttons to learn, no lives to count — just timing. This version keeps that rule and adds colour: a sunny desert, green cacti, purple pterodactyls, and a dino that ducks, jumps, and trips with a little more personality than the pixel original.

ol: Jump late, not early. A jump from too far away lands you on top of the cactus — wait until it is close, then tap.
Duck, do not jump, the low birds. A low pterodactyl flies at head height: jumping into it is the most common way to end a run.
Run under the high birds. If a bird is flying well above the dino's head, keep running — jumping under it only risks landing on the next cactus.
Watch the gap after a cluster. Obstacles come in groups, and the second cactus often follows closer than the first — land, then jump again at once.
On a phone, use two thumbs. Left thumb holds DUCK, right thumb taps JUMP — that way a low bird right after a cactus costs you nothing.
Stay calm as it speeds up. The game gets faster, but the jumps stay the same height — the timing you learned at 1.0× still works at 2.0×, it just comes sooner.

p: For another one-more-go classic, flap through the pipes in [[flappy-bird]] or bounce up the platforms in [[doodle-jump]]. If you would rather test your aim than your timing, shoot the bubbles in [[bubble-shooter]]. You can find every fast, one-more-go game in [[cat:arcade|arcade games]].

faq: Press Space, Arrow Up, or W on a keyboard, tap the game area, or hit the big green JUMP button on a phone. The dino jumps as long as it is on the ground — you cannot double-jump in mid-air.
How do I duck under a bird?

Hold Arrow Down or S on a keyboard, or hold the DUCK button on a phone. The dino flattens itself until you let go. Ducking only helps against the low pterodactyls — the high ones fly above the dino's head anyway.
Do the high birds need jumping?
No. A high pterodactyl flies above the dino's head, so just keep running underneath it. Only the low birds need a duck, and only the cacti need a jump.

The dino starts at a gentle jog and speeds up with your score — about 20% faster at 100 points, and up to two and a half times the starting speed past 700 points. The jumps stay the same height throughout.
What happens when I hit a cactus?
